material_systems.name: Interior Adhesion Primer
material_systems.description: Water-based adhesion promoter for previously painted interior windows. Bonds to glossy, chalky, or oil-based existing coatings without full mechanical sanding. Primary RP primer for sound-to-peeling conditions. Windows historically received oil-based enamel for hardness/blocking resistance -- coating ID test is critical. Adhesion primer is MANDATORY when solvent test confirms alkyd base. For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: use only when adhesion test is marginal or existing coating is alkyd. For SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas, full prime if bare >30%. For SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime after complete scrape.

products.notes: Water-based for low VOC and easy cleanup. Bonds to glossy surfaces without full mechanical sanding. For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: use only when adhesion test is marginal or existing sheen is semi-gloss+. For SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas, full prime if bare >30%. For SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime after complete scrape. Window profiles (muntins, sash rabbets) require thorough coverage in recessed areas.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: conditional -- only when adhesion test marginal or existing coating is alkyd (solvent test confirms oil-based)
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas; full prime if bare >30% of surface
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime after complete scrape to sound substrate

material_systems.name: Interior Shellac Stain-Blocking Primer
material_systems.description: Shellac-based stain-blocking primer for smoke/nicotine-damaged interior windows. Shellac is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Full surface application required. Strong odor -- requires ventilation. Fast dry (~45 min recoat). NOT water-cleanup -- requires denatured alcohol for tool cleaning. Window mullion and sash crevices trap concentrated smoke deposits -- ensure full coverage of all profile details.

products.notes: Shellac is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Full surface application required. Strong odor -- requires ventilation. Fast dry (~45 min recoat). NOT water-cleanup -- requires denatured alcohol for tool cleaning. Window muntin intersections and sash crevices trap concentrated smoke deposits -- ensure full coverage of all profile details.

material_systems.cleanup: Denatured alcohol. Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. CON_DENATURED_ALCOHOL required.

material_systems.name: Interior Mildew-Resistant Primer
material_systems.description: Mildew-resistant primer with antimicrobial additives for moisture-damaged windows. Applied after biocide treatment and full drying. Windows are the #1 interior mildew site due to condensation on sills, jamb bottoms, and sash bottom rails. Gate condition: moisture SOURCE must be resolved and MC < 12% before painting.

products.notes: Apply after biocide treatment (24 hr dry) and confirmation that MC < 12%. Full surface application on all moisture-affected areas. Sill and sash bottom rail are primary targets. Antimicrobial additives prevent mildew recurrence under paint film. Water-based formula -- standard cleanup.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE: full surface on all moisture-affected areas -- sill, jamb bottoms, sash bottom rail at minimum

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Standard production acrylic enamel for QT3 window repaint. Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Waterborne alkyd or acrylic enamel preferred for windows due to superior blocking resistance on operable sashes. Standard acrylic has softer film than alkyd alternatives -- monitor for blocking on operable sash contact surfaces.

example_products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
products.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Standard production grade. Lower hardness than alkyd -- monitor for blocking on operable window sash contact surfaces. Latex topcoat over existing alkyd creates soft-on-hard interface prone to blocking -- adhesion primer recommended when existing paint is oil-based.

material_systems.notes: Standard production system for QT3 window RP. Satin is the only sheen available at QT3 per sheen/QT gate. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion on product selection (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Urethane-modified alkyd / waterbased alkyd for premium residential window repaint at QT4. Superior flow and leveling, harder cured film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Do not overwork. Blocking resistant -- ideal for operable window sashes. Extended cure time (7+ days full hardness) -- keep sashes ajar during cure.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
products.notes: Superior flow and leveling. Harder cured film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Do not overwork. Blocking resistant -- ideal for operable window sash contact surfaces. Extended cure time (7+ days full hardness) -- keep sashes ajar until fully cured.

material_systems.notes: Premium residential standard for QT4 window RP. Semi-gloss is traditional/default window sheen at this tier. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Premium acrylic-urethane enamel for superior window repaint at QT5. Maximum durability, excellent leveling, hardest film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Best blocking resistance of any waterborne system.

products.coat_notes: QT5 brush typically requires 3 coats per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 spray: 2 coats standard.
products.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Hardest film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Best blocking resistance of any waterborne system -- optimal for operable sashes. Sands easily between coats.

material_systems.notes: Premium/custom home standard for QT5 window RP. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion (RC-005).

ITM_WINDOW_UNIT.notes: Coverage based on medium window (~12 LF perimeter, ~9 SF equivalent painted surface including frame, sash, muntins). Previously painted substrate absorbs less primer than bare wood. Higher coverage than NC bare-wood primer (350-400 SF/gal). Range reflects size bucket variation: S bucket ~12 SF, M ~18 SF, L ~25 SF. TDL muntin windows have ~20% more surface area.

ITM_WINDOW_JAMB.notes: Extension jamb/reveal is a small surface per window. ~4 SF per jamb set (head + 2 sides). Not all windows have extension jambs. Previously painted surface -- higher coverage than bare wood.

coverage_profiles.notes: Adhesion primer on previously painted window surfaces. Lower porosity than bare wood results in higher coverage vs NC primer profiles (COV_WIN_PRIMER at 400 SF/gal bare wood). Window profiles (sash rabbets, muntin intersections, frame moldings) have recessed areas requiring thorough coverage.
assumptions: Previously painted substrate -- lower absorption than bare wood
Medium window: ~12 LF perimeter, ~18 SF painted surface equivalent
Size bucket and muntin modifiers affect EA-to-SF conversion but not SF/gal coverage rate

ITM_WINDOW_UNIT.notes: Shellac stain blocker has lower coverage than latex adhesion primer due to higher solids content. Full surface application required on smoke-damaged windows. Window muntin intersections and sash crevices trap concentrated smoke deposits -- ensure thorough coverage.

ITM_WINDOW_JAMB.notes: Shellac on jamb surfaces. Full surface application for smoke damage. Lower coverage than adhesion primer.

coverage_profiles.notes: Shellac-based stain blocker has lower coverage than latex primers due to higher solids content and heavier required film build. Full surface application required on smoke-damaged windows.
assumptions: Full surface application on smoke-damaged windows
Shellac products have higher solids, lower spread rate than latex
Window profiles require additional material in recessed areas

ITM_WINDOW_UNIT.notes: Mildew primer coverage similar to adhesion primer -- latex-based formula. Slightly lower than adhesion due to thicker recommended film build for antimicrobial effectiveness. Typically applied to sill and sash bottom areas primarily, but full surface recommended when mildew history is extensive.

ITM_WINDOW_JAMB.notes: Jamb bottom is a primary moisture damage site (water wicks into end grain). Full jamb priming recommended when moisture damage is present.

coverage_profiles.notes: Mildew-resistant primer coverage similar to adhesion primer (latex-based formula). Slightly thicker recommended film build for antimicrobial effectiveness. Windows are the #1 interior mildew site due to condensation -- sill and jamb bottoms are primary targets.
assumptions: Latex formula -- similar coverage to adhesion primer
Slightly thicker film build for antimicrobial effectiveness
Sill and sash bottom rail are primary moisture/mildew targets

ITM_WINDOW_UNIT.notes: Finish coat on primed/prepared window surface via brush. Equivalent to NC finish coverage (COV_WIN_FINISH at 400 SF/gal) because substrate condition after prime/prep is equivalent. Brush application has minimal waste vs spray. TDL windows use more material due to additional muntin surface area (~20% more).

ITM_WINDOW_JAMB.notes: Jamb finish coat. Small surface area per jamb -- material consumption is minimal relative to window unit.

coverage_profiles.notes: Finish coat coverage on primed window surfaces via brush application. Equivalent to NC (COV_WIN_FINISH) because substrate condition after prep/prime is equivalent to NC after prime. Coat count: QT3-QT4 = 2 coats, QT5 brush = 3 coats per FFD 15.10.3.
assumptions: Primed smooth surface -- equivalent to NC after prime
Medium window: ~18 SF painted surface equivalent
Two-coat system standard; third coat at QT5 brush has same per-coat coverage
TDL muntin windows have ~20% more surface area -- lower effective ea_per_gallon

ITM_WINDOW_UNIT.notes: Spray finish on primed window surface. Base coverage rate equivalent to brush (400 SF/gal) but overspray waste factor of 20-40% reduces effective coverage per gallon. Window profiles (sash rabbets, muntins) cause higher overspray than flat surfaces. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.2.2.

ITM_WINDOW_JAMB.notes: Spray finish on jamb. Recessed jamb profile captures more overspray than flat surfaces.

coverage_profiles.notes: Spray finish coverage includes 20-40% waste factor for overspray per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.2.2. Window profiles (3D sash, muntin intersections) cause higher overspray than flat trim. Spray method is rare for RP windows (breakeven at ~8-12 windows).
assumptions: Base coverage rate equivalent to brush -- waste factor accounts for overspray
Window 3D profiles cause higher waste than flat surfaces

consumables.name: RP Assessment Kit (adhesion test + coating ID)
consumables.specification: Cross-hatch cutter, pressure-sensitive tape (ASTM D3359), mineral spirits, white rags for coating identification solvent test, moisture meter
consumables.notes: RP-specific assessment supplies. One kit per project. Includes ASTM D3359 cross-hatch adhesion test materials, solvent test supplies for latex vs oil-based coating identification, and moisture meter for sill/jamb MC readings. Windows historically received oil-based enamel -- coating ID is critical. Moisture check is especially important for windows (condensation damage site). Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: TSP (Trisodium Phosphate) Cleaner
consumables.specification: Powdered or liquid TSP concentrate, mixed per manufacturer directions
consumables.notes: RP window decontamination wash. Removes kitchen grease, bathroom humidity residue, hand oils on sash handles, and airborne pollutants from existing paint. Windows accumulate contaminants on horizontal sill surfaces. One quart of concentrate makes enough solution for ~40 windows (windows are smaller than door openings -- higher yield per quart). Rinse thoroughly -- TSP residue interferes with acrylic curing. Not used in NC (new substrate is clean). Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Deglosser
consumables.specification: Liquid sander/deglosser for chemical degloss of existing paint, Krud Kutter Gloss-Off or equivalent
consumables.notes: RP-specific: chemical degloss for existing semi-gloss/gloss window paint. Dulls existing sheen to promote adhesion without full mechanical sanding. One quart covers ~20 windows (windows are smaller surface area than doors -- higher yield). Especially useful on complex window profiles (muntins, sash rabbets, frame moldings) where mechanical sanding cannot reach all recessed areas. Not used in NC. Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Wood Hardener / Consolidant
consumables.specification: Penetrating wood consolidant, Minwax Wood Hardener or equivalent
consumables.notes: For moisture-damaged window sills and sash bottom rails where wood substrate is softened by condensation. Penetrating consolidant stabilizes wood fibers before filling/priming. One pint treats ~10 window sill/sash bottom sections. Conditional on SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE + soft substrate finding during assessment. Windows are the #1 interior condensation damage site. Not used in NC (no moisture-damaged substrate). Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Mildewcide / Biocide Solution
consumables.specification: Commercial mildewcide solution or bleach-water solution (1:3 ratio) for mildew kill treatment
consumables.notes: For mildew treatment on moisture-damaged window sills and jamb bottoms. Windows are the #1 interior mildew site due to condensation. Apply to all affected areas, allow 24 hr dry before priming. One quart treats ~20 windows (mildew is typically localized to sill/sash bottom areas). Conditional on SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE with visible mildew. Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Glazing Compound (Acrylic or DAP)
consumables.specification: Acrylic glazing compound or DAP 33 glazing, for spot repair of failed glazing on older windows
consumables.notes: Window-specific RP consumable for spot repair of failed/cracked glazing compound on older single-pane and TDL windows. Remove failed sections, apply fresh compound, tool smooth. Acrylic glazing is paintable within 3-7 days. Not applicable to modern IG (insulated glass) units. Not used in NC (factory-installed glazing). One quart covers ~15 windows for spot repair (<20% of glazing perimeter).

consumables.name: Glass Scraper (Single-Edge Razor Tool)
consumables.specification: Handled glass scraper with replaceable single-edge razor blades
consumables.notes: For post-cure glass cleaning -- remove paint from glass panes after masking teardown. Handled scraper is more ergonomic than loose razor blades for extended glass cleaning. One per crew, reusable. Replace blades frequently for clean cuts. Use with CON_RAZOR_BLADE for blade supply.

consumables.name: Single-edge razor blade
consumables.usage: Replacement blades for glass scraper cleanup after cure
consumables.notes: Sharp razor for scraping excess paint from glass during cleanup. Replace frequently for clean cuts. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.1.1. One blade per ~5 medium windows.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 120-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 120 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: Aggressive grit for feathering scrape edges on failing/peeling windows. Creates smooth transition from scraped to sound paint at sash bottom rails, meeting rails, sill failure points. One sheet covers ~5 windows for scrape edge feathering (smaller surface area per EA than doors).

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 150 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: General prep grit for degloss scuff sanding and mechanical surface preparation on sound paint. All tiers. One sheet per ~6 windows for mechanical degloss (smaller surface per EA than doors). Used on flat frame faces and sash stiles.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 180-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 180 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: Fine prep grit for light scuff sanding on sound paint surfaces. Intermediate between 150 and 220. Suitable for degloss scuff on satin-sheen existing paint. One sheet per ~6 windows.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 220 grit, 9x11 inch

grit_by_tier.QT3: 220 -- spot sand nibs and rough spots only
grit_by_tier.QT4: 220 -- full surface sand for adhesion and leveling

consumables.notes: Interstage sanding between finish coats. Spot sand at QT3, full surface at QT4. Also used for light sand of primer before finish. One sheet per ~5 windows for interstage sanding. Rigid sanding block mandatory for flat surfaces per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 320 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: QT5 interstage sanding between finish coats. Thorough 320-grit sanding per FFD 15.10.3. Uniform scratch pattern required. One sheet per ~4 windows (more thorough sanding at QT5). Rigid sanding block mandatory per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.specification: Rigid sanding block, fine grit range (150-320)
consumables.notes: Rigid blocks remove defects -- mandatory per FFD 15.4.1 for between-coat sanding on flat window surfaces (frame jamb flats, sash stile flats). Flexible sponges are NOT acceptable for defect leveling. One block per crew, reusable across coats and windows.

consumables.name: Contour Sanding Sponge
consumables.specification: Flexible sanding sponge, medium/fine grit (150-220), angled edges for profile conformance
consumables.notes: Flexible sanding sponge for window profile prep and interstage. Conforms to sash rabbets, muntin intersections, frame molding profiles where rigid blocks cannot reach. Essential for TDL muntin windows. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine: flexible sponges for profile-following only, NOT for defect leveling (use rigid block for flat surfaces). One sponge per ~12 windows.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (1.5 inch)
consumables.specification: 1.5 inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle (nylon/polyester blend)
consumables.notes: Primary brush for window detail work (sash, muntins, frame details). 1.5-inch per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.2.1. Smaller than trim/door brush (2-2.5 inch) for detailed window profiles. One per painter per material change (primer brush + finish brush).

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5 inch)
consumables.specification: 2-2.5 inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle (nylon/polyester blend)
consumables.notes: Secondary brush for larger window frame surfaces and extension jamb. One per painter. Also used for touch-up/detail with spray method.

consumables.name: Brush for shellac (dedicated)
consumables.specification: 2-inch angled sash brush, dedicated for shellac use, natural or synthetic bristle
consumables.notes: Dedicated brush for shellac stain-blocking primer (BIN). Shellac requires alcohol cleanup -- keep separate from latex brushes. Conditional on smoke damage substrate state. Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411 (fine finish)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 310-411 range (6-8 inch fan, 0.010-0.011 orifice) for fine-finish window work
consumables.notes: Fine-finish spray tips for windows. Tight fan pattern for window work. Fine atomization for smooth finish. One tip per ~50 windows. Replace when pattern degrades.

consumables.name: Spray gun filter
consumables.specification: In-line filter for airless spray gun
consumables.notes: Replace when clogged or every ~50 gallons. One per spray setup.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.specification: Resin-impregnated cheesecloth for dust removal
consumables.notes: Wipe window surfaces immediately before each coat application to remove sanding dust. Essential for quality finish per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.12. One tack cloth covers ~8 medium windows. Use before every coat for dust-free surface.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackling compound
consumables.specification: Lightweight spackling compound, tub or squeeze tube
consumables.notes: For patching scrape edges, filling gouges, and repairing defects revealed after degloss/scrape on RP windows. GOOD condition typically has no fill work. FAIR/POOR condition: fill scraped transition areas, small defects on sash and frame. One quart per ~30 windows (smaller fill areas per EA than doors).

consumables.name: Flexible putty knife
consumables.specification: Flexible putty knife, 1.5-inch
consumables.notes: For applying lightweight spackle to defects and scrape edges, and for glazing compound application. Flexible blade for flush fill on window surfaces. One per crew, reusable.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.specification: Paintable acrylic latex caulk, white, 10.1 oz tube
consumables.notes: For caulk assess/replace at window frame-to-wall joints and extension jamb joints on RP windows. RP caulk replacement is selective -- assess each joint, replace only deteriorated sections. ~12 windows per tube because partial re-caulk (shorter perimeter than doors). Allow cure time before coating.

consumables.name: Caulk gun
consumables.specification: Standard caulk gun, ratchet-type
consumables.notes: Reusable tool for caulk application. One per crew.

consumables.name: Blue painter's tape 1.5-inch
consumables.specification: Blue painter's tape, 1.5-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: For glass edge masking, wall masking, hardware masking, sill edge masking, and attaching masking paper/film. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 180 LF (60 yards) per roll. Primary masking tape for all window protection tasks. RP requires wall masking for BOTH brush and spray (walls are finished in occupied homes).

consumables.name: Glass masking film/paper
consumables.specification: Pre-taped masking film or masking paper cut to pane size
consumables.notes: Cover glass panes to protect from paint. Mandatory for all windows regardless of application method. Largest single protection task (30-40% of total time on TDL windows). Transfers DIRECT from NC.

consumables.name: Masking paper 12-inch
consumables.specification: Masking paper, 12-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: Wall masking adjacent to window during spray AND brush methods (RP: walls are finished -- masking required for both methods unlike NC where brush skips wall masking). 12-inch width covers wall adjacent to window frame perimeter. Attached with blue tape.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.specification: Canvas drop cloth, 4x12 ft runner or 4x5 ft compact
consumables.notes: Floor protection in window work area for brush method drip containment. Runner-style positioned under window. 1-2 per painter, reusable. RP always has finished floors -- floor protection is mandatory.

consumables.name: Rosin paper
consumables.specification: Rosin paper roll, 36-inch width, 500 SF per roll
consumables.notes: 8-foot radius floor protection for spray overspray containment around each window. Per PS_PROTECT_SF.FLOOR_8FT_RADIUS input. Taped at seams and edges with blue tape.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 4 mil
consumables.specification: 4 mil plastic sheeting for furniture/window treatment protection
consumables.notes: RP-specific: furniture and window treatment protection in occupied homes. Drape over furniture near windows, cover window treatments (curtains, blinds) that cannot be removed. Heavier weight (4 mil) prevents tear during work. Both spray and brush methods may need furniture protection in occupied homes.

consumables.name: Zip-lock bags for hardware
consumables.specification: Gallon-size zip-lock bags for hardware storage and labeling
consumables.notes: For bagging and labeling removed window hardware (locks, latches, crank operators). One bag per window when hardware is removed. Label with window location for accurate reinstall. RP hardware may have paint buildup requiring scoring before removal.

consumables.name: Denatured alcohol
consumables.specification: Denatured alcohol for shellac cleanup
consumables.notes: Required for cleaning brushes and tools used with shellac stain-blocking primer (BIN). Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. One quart per project. Conditional on smoke damage substrate state. Shared across interior RP specs.

floor_perimeter.description: Drop cloth runners along window work area for brush method drip containment

floor_full_8ft_radius.description: Full radial floor coverage around window spray zone for overspray containment

glass_mask.description: Paper/film masking on all window glass panes -- MANDATORY regardless of method
glass_mask.condition: ALWAYS -- mandatory regardless of application method

hardware_covers.description: Tape/bag or remove window hardware (locks, latches, crank operators)
hardware_covers.condition: ALWAYS -- mandatory. RP hardware may have paint buildup requiring scoring before removal.
hardware_covers.notes: Brush: mask hardware with tape. Spray: remove hardware, bag, label, reinstall after cure. Method-dependent protection strategy.

wall_adjacent_window.description: Wall masking around window perimeter -- RP requires BOTH brush and spray (walls are finished)
wall_adjacent_window.condition: ALWAYS for RP -- walls are finished in occupied homes. MODIFIED from NC: NC only requires wall masking for spray.

furniture_adjacent.description: Cover or move furniture and window treatments near windows in occupied homes
furniture_adjacent.condition: RP-specific -- occupied homes have furniture and window treatments near windows
furniture_adjacent.notes: Window treatments (curtains, blinds, valances) removed or pinned/covered. Furniture within work zone covered with plastic. Not present in NC. Shared with other interior RP specs.

required_inputs.purpose: Small window count for size bucket modifier
Total window count for per-project fixed-time tasks and material totals
Wall masking LF around window perimeter -- RP requires for BOTH methods
Surface condition (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) for prep intensity modifier
Pre-1978 flag for RRP lead-safe containment module

compatibility_rules.description: Adhesion primer under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Water-based adhesion primer is compatible with all fine-finish topcoat chemistries. Scuff sand primer before finish coats.

compatibility_rules.description: Shellac stain blocker under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac seals stains and is compatible with all topcoat chemistries. Universal undercoat. No latex alternative for smoke/nicotine stains.

compatibility_rules.description: Mildew primer under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Latex-based mildew primer is compatible with all fine-finish topcoat chemistries.

compatibility_rules.description: No primer needed for SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT with good adhesion + latex existing coating
compatibility_rules.notes: When adhesion test passes (ASTM D3359 rating 4B or 5B), existing coating is latex (solvent test confirms), and paint is sound -- no primer is required. Degloss/scuff and apply finish directly. This is the most common residential window repaint scenario (cosmetic refresh).

compatibility_rules.description: Adhesion primer mandatory for alkyd existing coating
compatibility_rules.notes: Latex finish over un-primed alkyd coating WILL fail. Adhesion primer (SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT) is mandatory when solvent test confirms oil-based existing paint. No exceptions. Windows historically received alkyd enamel -- coating ID is critical.

compatibility_rules.description: Shellac BIN is the only acceptable primer for smoke/nicotine damage
compatibility_rules.notes: No latex alternative reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Shellac BIN is mandatory for SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE. Do not substitute with latex stain-blocking primer.
Semi-gloss requires QT4+. Gloss requires QT5. Satin available at all tiers. Flat/matte/eggshell NOT valid for windows per Fine_Finish_Doctrine.

If moisture meter reads MC > 15% on sill, jamb bottoms, or sash bottom rail -- STOP. Do not proceed to prime until moisture source is resolved and substrate dried to MC < 12%. Painting over wet substrate causes premature failure.

compatibility_rules.description: Block-resistant coating recommended for operable sash
compatibility_rules.notes: Operable sashes have friction/contact surfaces. Block-resistant coatings (modified urethane at QT4+, premium urethane at QT5) are strongly recommended. Standard acrylic enamel (QT3) has softer film -- higher blocking risk. Keep sashes ajar for 3-7 day cure per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 10.1.

compatibility_rules.description: Modified urethane finish over previously painted surface
compatibility_rules.notes: Modified urethane finish coats adhere well to deglossed/primed existing coatings. Adhesion primer recommended when existing coating is oil-based or high-sheen.

risk_notes.risk: Freshly painted operable windows stuck closed due to insufficient cure time. RP compounds risk because existing paint buildup narrows clearance and latex-over-alkyd creates soft-on-hard interface.
risk_notes.mitigation: Paint sashes in AJAR position. Allow 3-7 day cure before closing. Use urethane-enriched enamels (QT4+) for blocking resistance. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 10.1.

risk_notes.risk: Interior windows historically received oil-based (alkyd) enamel for hardness and blocking resistance. Latex over un-primed oil-based coating will fail, especially at friction surfaces (sash meeting rails, frame-to-sash contact).
risk_notes.mitigation: Always perform coating ID test (solvent rub) during assessment. If alkyd/oil identified, adhesion primer (SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT) is mandatory. Never skip primer over oil-based existing paint.

risk_notes.risk: Windows are the HIGHEST RISK surface for lead exposure in residential buildings. Operable sashes are friction surfaces -- wood-on-wood contact generates fine lead-containing dust. This is the #1 lead dust exposure pathway.
risk_notes.mitigation: MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT module is conditional on PS_META.BOOL.HOME_PRE_1978. RRP-certified renovator required. Containment, HEPA vacuum, and wet methods per EPA RRP Rule. Windows require enhanced containment due to friction surface dust generation.

risk_notes.topic: Condensation/moisture damage on sills and sash bottoms
risk_notes.risk: Windows are the #1 interior moisture damage site. Condensation runs down glass and pools on sill/sash bottom. Water wicks into end grain, causing paint bubbling, mildew, and substrate softening. Painting over wet or mildewed substrate causes premature failure.
risk_notes.mitigation: Moisture check during assessment (MC must be < 12% before priming). Resolve moisture source. Biocide treatment for mildew (24 hr dry). Wood hardener for softened substrate. Mildew-resistant primer (SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT).

risk_notes.risk: Overworking modified urethane products causes roping/brush marks on window surfaces. Window detail areas (muntins, sash rabbets) increase risk of overworking.
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Do not go back and rework. Sand marks out between coats with rigid block. Use 1.5-inch brush for detail areas to control coating delivery.

risk_notes.topic: Glass masking incomplete -- paint on glass
risk_notes.risk: Incomplete glass masking results in paint on glass requiring post-cure scraping. TDL windows with many panes are especially prone to masking gaps at tape edges.
risk_notes.mitigation: Thorough glass masking with pre-taped film or paper. Verify all tape edges are sealed before coating. Post-cure glass scraping with razor tool is standard cleanup. Budget 30-40% of total time for glass masking on TDL windows.

material_notes.selection_guidance: Material system selection follows Fine Finish Doctrine: QT3 = SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, QT4 = SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, QT5 = SYS_FF_PREMIUM. Window unit and extension jamb use the same finish system. RP primer selection is state-driven (adhesion, stain-block, or mildew) and independent of finish system selection. Waterborne alkyd or urethane enamels are preferred for windows due to blocking resistance on operable sashes.
material_notes.coverage_variability: Window coverage is EA-based (medium window unit ~18 SF equivalent, extension jamb ~4 SF). Size bucket modifiers affect SF per EA: S=0.75x, M=1.00x, L=1.40x. TDL windows have ~20% more surface area due to muntins.
material_notes.rp_vs_nc_differences: RP uses state-driven RP primers (SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT, SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT, SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT) instead of NC substrate-driven primers (SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_ACRYLIC, SYS_PRIMER_ALUMINUM_DTM, etc.). RP primer coverage is higher than NC because previously painted surfaces absorb less. RP adds TSP wash, deglosser, assessment kit, biocide, glazing compound, wood hardener, and contour sanding sponges not needed in NC. Wall masking is required for BOTH methods in RP (NC only masks walls for spray).
material_notes.open_time_by_chemistry: Standard acrylic enamel has moderate open time. Modified urethane/waterborne alkyd (Advance, Emerald Urethane) has SHORT open time (5-10 min) -- do not overwork per FFD 15.3.1.
material_notes.coat_count_summary: QT3-QT4: 2 finish coats standard. QT5 brush: 3 finish coats per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 spray: 2 finish coats. Prime coat (when applicable) is always 1 coat.
material_notes.blocking_note: Operable window sashes are the most blocking-sensitive interior surface. Standard acrylic enamel (QT3) has softest film -- use with caution on DH/casement/slider sashes. Modified urethane (QT4) and premium urethane (QT5) have progressively harder films and better blocking resistance.

assumptions.value: Medium window unit = ~18 SF painted surface equivalent (frame + sash + muntins), extension jamb = ~4 SF
assumptions.source: Size bucket perimeter math (Area ~ P^2/16) + window component surface area estimates
assumptions.note: Medium window ~12 LF perimeter. S=~12 SF, M=~18 SF, L=~25 SF. TDL adds ~20% for muntin surface area.

assumptions.value: RP adhesion primer at 425 SF/gal vs NC bare-wood primer at 350-400 SF/gal
assumptions.source: Previously painted surfaces absorb less primer than bare wood
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines RP vs NC primer coverage differential. Derived from product PDS typical coverage range and field practice. Consistent with door RP materials (COV_DIRP_PRIMER_ADHESION at 425 SF/gal).

assumptions.source: Field practice estimate -- windows are smaller than door openings
assumptions.note: TSP yield higher per quart for windows than doors (~30/qt) because window surface area per EA is smaller.
Window 3D profiles (sash rabbets, muntin intersections) cause higher overspray than flat surfaces.

assumptions.value: 1 quart per ~15 windows for spot repair (<20% of glazing perimeter)
assumptions.note: Glazing compound repair is limited to older single-pane and TDL windows. Modern IG units have no exposed glazing. Yield varies widely by window age and condition.
